title: North Dakota At-Large U.S. House Election, 2026
description: This race is for North Dakota’s at-large seat in the U.S. House of Representatives, the state’s only congressional district. It matters because the winner will represent North Dakota on federal issues such as agriculture, energy, taxes, and federal spending. North Dakota has leaned Republican in recent federal elections, and the 2026 contest is expected to feature an incumbent Republican seeking reelection against Democratic-NPL and Republican primary challengers. The race is likely to turn on national political trends as well as local concerns about the economy, tariffs, and energy policy.
polling_note: No public polling found for this race as of 2026-04-29.

candidates.name: Julie Fedorchak
candidates.summary: Julie Fedorchak is the Republican U.S. representative for North Dakota’s at-large congressional district, first elected in 2024 and sworn in on January 3, 2025. Before Congress, she served on the North Dakota Public Service Commission from 2012 to 2025 and previously worked in state government and communications roles.

Healthcare.stance: Fedorchak says she supports affordable, high-quality health care, especially for rural areas, and favors patient-centered solutions that lower costs, expand access, and reduce government bureaucracy. Her House page says health care decisions should be made by doctors and patients in North Dakota, not Washington.

Climate/Energy.stance: Fedorchak says she is focused on energy affordability, reliability, sustainability, and security, and supports expanding domestic energy production while improving environmental stewardship. Her House materials emphasize unleashing American energy production, strengthening the grid, and supporting North Dakota’s role in feeding and fueling the country.

These bills require proof of U.S. citizenship for voter registration in federal elections and add a photo ID requirement to vote in federal elections, aligning with North Dakota's standards and aiming to strengthen election integrity.

candidates.voting_summary: Julie Fedorchak is an incumbent U.S. House member, serving North Dakota’s at-large district since Jan. 3, 2025. GovTrack shows her voting record as generally aligned with the Republican caucus, with key votes including yea on H.R. 6500 (AGOA Extension Act), yea on H.R. 2483 (SUPPORT for Patients and Communities Reauthorization Act of 2025), yea on H.R. 1263 (Strengthening the Quad Act), and nay on H.R. 1917 (Great Lakes Mass Marking Program Act of 2025).

FollowTheMoney also has a state-level entity page for Julie A. Liffrig-Fedorchak, but the accessible page text here does not surface donor totals or top contributors; based on the available OpenSecrets profile, the best-supported sector-level takeaway is that her fundraising is tracked through federal disclosures and industry/PAC categories rather than a single dominant small-donor source.

forecast.rationale: No public polling exists for this race, so confidence is low. However, the structural factors strongly favor the Republican incumbent. North Dakota is a deeply Republican state — Trump won it by roughly 35 points in 2024, and the at-large House seat has been held by Republicans since 2011. Incumbent Julie Fedorchak, first elected in 2024 with about 67% of the vote, has the advantages of incumbency and prior statewide experience (12 years on the North Dakota Public Service Commission). Her Democratic-NPL challenger, Trygve Hammer, has no detailed public profile or donor data available in the race file, suggesting limited campaign infrastructure. A Republican primary challenger (Alex Balazs) is listed but poses minimal general-election risk. Given the district's strong Republican lean and incumbency advantage, Republicans are clearly favored, though the absence of any public polling prevents a 'safe' classification.
